title: "Forecasting U.S. Monthly Retail and Food-Service Sales"
subtitle: "Team analysis code (Appendix 1)"
author: "Imogen Ronde, Ryan Salas, Christopher Guillen"
format: html

---

**How to run:** Requires R with the tidyverse, fpp3, and gt packages. Data is read from `MRTSSM44X72USN_snapshot.csv` in the same folder, a snapshot of FRED series MRTSSM44X72USN downloaded on November 28, 2026. If the snapshot file is missing, the code downloads the series from FRED and saves a new snapshot (this requires an internet connection, and values may differ slightly because the Census Bureau revises past months). Click Render to run all chunks in order.

**AI disclosure:** Portions of this script were drafted and combined with assistance from Claude (Anthropic). The team reviewed, ran, and verified all code and results.

```{r}
#| message: false
#| warning: false
library(tidyverse)
library(fpp3)
library(gt)
```

## Data

```{r}
# data snapshot of FRED series MRTSSM44X72USN (retail trade and food services),
# saved so results don't change when the Census Bureau revises past values
snapshot_file <- "MRTSSM44X72USN_snapshot.csv"

if (file.exists(snapshot_file)) {
  raw <- read_csv(snapshot_file, show_col_types = FALSE)
} else {
  url <- "https://fred.stlouisfed.org/graph/fredgraph.csv?id=MRTSSM44X72USN"
  raw <- read_csv(url, show_col_types = FALSE)
  write_csv(raw, snapshot_file)
}
names(raw)[1:2] <- c("DATE", "Sales")

# keep data through August 2026
retail <- raw |>
  mutate(DATE = as.Date(DATE), Month = yearmonth(DATE),
         Sales = parse_number(as.character(Sales))) |>
  select(Month, Sales) |>
  filter(Month <= yearmonth("2026 Aug")) |>
  filter(!is.na(Sales)) |>
  as_tsibble(index = Month)

# data quality checks
stopifnot(!any(is.na(retail$Sales)))
stopifnot(nrow(retail) == length(seq(min(retail$Month), max(retail$Month), by = 1)))
stopifnot(!any(retail$Sales <= 0))
```

## Train/Test Split

```{r}
# hold out the final 12 months for testing (Sep 2025 - Aug 2026)
test_start <- max(retail$Month) - 11
training <- retail |> filter(Month < test_start)
testing <- retail |> filter(Month >= test_start)
```

## Exploratory Data Analysis

```{r}
# Figure 1: full time series
retail |>
  autoplot(Sales) +
  labs(title = "U.S. Monthly Retail and Food-Service Sales, 1992–2026",
       y = "Sales (millions of US dollars)") +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::comma)

# Figure 2: seasonal plot
retail |>
  gg_season(Sales, labels = "none") +
  labs(title = "Seasonal Pattern by Year",
       y = "Sales (millions of US dollars)") +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::comma)

# Figure 3: STL decomposition
retail |>
  model(STL(Sales)) |>
  components() |>
  autoplot() +
  labs(title = "STL Decomposition of Retail Sales")
```

```{r}
# transformation and differencing checks (training data only)
training |> features(Sales, features = guerrero)
training |> features(Sales, unitroot_nsdiffs)
training |> features(difference(Sales, 12), unitroot_ndiffs)
```

## Model Selection: Auto TSLM

```{r}
# auto TSLM: let AICc choose the number of Fourier terms (K = 1 to 6)
fourier_search <- training |>
  model(
    K1 = TSLM(Sales ~ trend() + fourier(K = 1)),
    K2 = TSLM(Sales ~ trend() + fourier(K = 2)),
    K3 = TSLM(Sales ~ trend() + fourier(K = 3)),
    K4 = TSLM(Sales ~ trend() + fourier(K = 4)),
    K5 = TSLM(Sales ~ trend() + fourier(K = 5)),
    K6 = TSLM(Sales ~ trend() + fourier(K = 6))
  )

fourier_search |>
  glance() |>
  select(.model, adj_r_squared, AICc) |>
  arrange(AICc)
```

## Fit All Models

```{r}
# all models fit on the same training data
# ETS(M,A,M) was both the hand-picked and the auto-selected ETS model,
# so a single ETS model represents both
all_fits <- training |>
  model(
    Manual_ARIMA = ARIMA(Sales ~ 0 + pdq(1, 1, 1) + PDQ(0, 1, 1, period = 12)),
    Auto_ARIMA = ARIMA(Sales),
    ETS_MAM = ETS(Sales ~ error("M") + trend("A") + season("M")),
    Manual_TSLM = TSLM(log(Sales) ~ trend() + season()),
    Auto_TSLM = TSLM(Sales ~ trend() + fourier(K = 6)),
    Seasonal_Naive = SNAIVE(Sales)
  )

# selected orders for the auto ARIMA and the ETS parameters
all_fits |> select(Auto_ARIMA) |> report()
all_fits |> select(ETS_MAM) |> report()
```

## Test-Set Results

```{r}
# forecast the 12-month test period
all_fc <- all_fits |> forecast(new_data = testing)

# Table 1: test-set accuracy for all models
all_fc |>
  accuracy(retail) |>
  select(.model, RMSE, MAE, MAPE) |>
  arrange(RMSE) |>
  gt() |>
  tab_header(title = "Test-Set Forecast Accuracy by Model",
             subtitle = "Test period: Sep 2025 – Aug 2026") |>
  cols_label(.model = "Model", MAPE = "MAPE (%)") |>
  fmt_number(columns = c(RMSE, MAE), decimals = 0) |>
  fmt_number(columns = MAPE, decimals = 2) |>
  tab_source_note("RMSE and MAE in millions of US dollars")
```

```{r}
# Figure 4: test-period forecasts vs. actual sales (no intervals for clarity)
all_fc |>
  filter(.model %in% c("Manual_ARIMA", "ETS_MAM", "Manual_TSLM", "Seasonal_Naive")) |>
  autoplot(retail |> filter_index("2025 Jan" ~ .), level = NULL) +
  labs(title = "Test-Period Forecasts vs. Actual Sales",
       x = NULL, y = "Sales (millions of US dollars)",
       colour = "Model") +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::comma) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

## Residual Diagnostics

```{r}
# residual checks for the manual ARIMA
all_fits |> select(Manual_ARIMA) |> gg_tsresiduals()

# Ljung-Box test (dof = 3 estimated ARIMA coefficients: ar1, ma1, sma1)
all_fits |>
  select(Manual_ARIMA) |>
  augment() |>
  features(.innov, ljung_box, lag = 24, dof = 3)
```

## Rolling-Origin Cross-Validation (Log TSLM)

```{r}
#| warning: false
# rolling origin: start with 20 years of data, add 1 year per fold
retail_cv <- retail |>
  stretch_tsibble(.init = 240, .step = 12)

cv_fc <- retail_cv |>
  model(Manual_TSLM = TSLM(log(Sales) ~ trend() + season())) |>
  forecast(h = 12)

# overall cross-validated accuracy
cv_fc |> accuracy(retail) |> select(.model, RMSE, MAE, MAPE)

# Figure 5: accuracy for each fold
fold_start <- cv_fc |>
  as_tibble() |>
  group_by(.id) |>
  summarise(Start = min(Month))

cv_by_fold <- cv_fc |>
  accuracy(retail, by = c(".model", ".id")) |>
  left_join(fold_start, by = ".id")

cv_by_fold |>
  ggplot(aes(x = Start, y = MAPE)) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_point() +
  labs(title = "Rolling-Origin CV: 12-Month Forecast Error by Year",
       x = "Forecast start", y = "MAPE (%)")
```

## Final Forecast

```{r}
# final 12-month forecast (Sep 2026 – Aug 2027) using the best model refit on all data
final_fit <- retail |>
  model(Manual_ARIMA = ARIMA(Sales ~ 0 + pdq(1, 1, 1) + PDQ(0, 1, 1, period = 12)))

final_fc <- final_fit |> forecast(h = 12)

# Figure 6: final forecast with 80% and 95% prediction intervals
final_fc |>
  autoplot(retail |> filter_index("2023 Jan" ~ .), level = c(80, 95)) +
  labs(title = "12-Month Retail Sales Forecast, Sep 2026 – Aug 2027",
       x = NULL, y = "Sales (millions of US dollars)") +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::comma) +
  theme_minimal()

# Table 2: monthly point forecasts
final_fc |>
  as_tibble() |>
  mutate(Month = as.character(Month)) |>
  select(Month, .mean) |>
  gt() |>
  tab_header(title = "Forecast Retail and Food-Service Sales",
             subtitle = "Manual ARIMA(1,1,1)(0,1,1)[12], Sep 2026 – Aug 2027") |>
  cols_label(.mean = "Forecast Sales") |>
  fmt_number(columns = .mean, decimals = 0) |>
  tab_source_note("Sales in millions of US dollars")
```
